access-and-save-framing: The pair describes capability and byte domains. Keep the native save-thread request, serializer, finalization and reference readers separate from offline decoding and durability. The original SFTR exact-name factory registry has separate registration, loader lookup and shutdown entries. The paired type-7 PCM writer and reader preserve two keyed maps and seed state. Type 9 has a distinct destination frame.
cargo: Separate mode-0 readiness and mode-1 charge from the movement controller and voyage completion. Timer conversion and hold capacity have independent producers.
construction: The catalogue discovery walk and selected construction gate have separate entries. Placement success does not follow from menu discovery or a preview predicate. The final status fold separates location restriction, budget and category quota. The automatic snap wrapper and replace/remove/add executor are separate.
containers-and-displays: Distinguish inventory rows, displayed world references and equipment. Save writer, loader and fixup are distinct, and source slot eligibility is conditional.
crew-and-robots: Keep menu capacity, ordinary assignment, script bypass, robot quota and active modifier contribution separate. Shared assignment machinery alone does not establish contribution.
defense: The mapped damage indicator and repair route have native entries. Encounter opportunity and authored eligibility also depend on shipped scripts and records outside this catalogue.
fabrication: The generic selector and manufactured catalogue callback differ from the shared producer scheduler. Preset products, admitted recipes and reachable ingredient stock are separate.
identity: The GetWorkshop callback is historically a LAB label. Preserve its registration/tail-jump boundary separately from the keyed target and the reverse member walk.
inorganic-production: Distinguish point admission, the registered resource key and elapsed production. Effective power and halt checks do not turn an inventory output into a placement result.
locations-ui: The registry adapter, selected-body refresh and summary field providers have separate identities. A listed row does not enumerate every outpost or expose a stable SFSE interface.
nominal-biomes: The discrete base lookup and nominal coverage calculation use separate routes. Terrain cells and layer resource-population coverage have different scopes.
organic-production: The selector, knowledge predicate, selection application and current ingredient consumption stay separate. A visible candidate does not prove known status or current production.
position: Original frame-restore and overlay helpers provide entry locators. Save-local joins, geographic anchors and the exact current reference position remain separate.
power: Effective contribution, graph traversal and allocation are separate. The original follow-up corrects queue/discovery-vector ordering and the load result stays sample-scoped.
resource-generation: The provider and the availability consumer have separate entries. Call-site examples, lock transitions and exclusive cache-lookup instructions remain locators within their respective functions. The original inactive-weight setting chain distinguishes initialized values, loaded DATA and the separate text-command mutation route. The scheduling chain keeps completion publication, dependency removal, ready scan and actual dispatch separate. The provider's caller-owned list append and cleanup have distinct source-lifetime limits.
shared-storage: Fixture recognition, the player-side backing reference and downstream spending remain separate. The add-on namespace stays independently pinned.
storage-and-output-links: Effective capacity, current weight, ordered endpoint admission and inventory movement have separate entries. Link topology does not prove actual transfer.
stored-resources: Keep provider registration, collection and asynchronous presentation separate from the underlying stock, with no new save persistence implication. The shared queued receiver sorts resource entries and inserts each count at the same index before the native binder exposes both arrays.
